q1: How much squash have you played on a proper court?
q1a: None yet, or only a handful of times.
q1b: Less than a year, or only now and then.
q1c: 1 to 2 years, about once a week or more.
q1d: More than 2 years of regular play, now or in the past.
q2: Have you played racketball, badminton, tennis, padel or another racket sport?
q2b: Yes, casually or a long time ago.
q2c: Yes, regularly for a year or more.
q2d: Yes — racketball, badminton or tennis in leagues, club teams or tournaments.
q3: Hitting length (drives to the back of the court) — which is closest to you?
q3a: I often hit the tin or miss the ball, and rallies rarely last more than a few shots.
q3b: I can keep a rally going, but my drives usually land short or bounce back off the back wall into the middle of the court.
q3c: My forehand drive usually dies at the back close to the side wall; my backhand gets deep but often comes out towards the middle.
q3d: I hit tight, straight length on both sides, also on the volley and when under pressure, and I vary height and pace on purpose.
q4: When the ball goes into a back corner — which is closest to you?
q4a: I usually can't get it back, especially once it has come off the back wall.
q4b: I get some back, often by hitting it up into the back wall or with a scrappy boast, but many go into the tin or straight to my opponent.
q4c: I return most of them with a drive to length or a boast; from deep in the backhand corner under pressure my return is often loose.
q4d: From either back corner I choose between a straight drive, a crosscourt and a boast, and I can still hit length out of the backhand corner under pressure.
q5: Volleys and the front of the court — what can you do reliably?
q5a: I let almost every ball bounce and don't play drop shots yet.
q5b: I volley balls that come straight at me and try the odd drop shot, but my drops often hit the tin or sit up in the middle.
q5c: I volley to cut off balls before they reach the back, and my straight drop from the front usually stays low near the side wall.
q5d: I hit volley drives and volley drops to take time away from my opponent, play tight drops and counter-drops, and lob to the back when I'm stretched at the front.
q6: Which games do you usually play, and how do they go?
q6a: Mostly lessons, coaching or hitting on my own — I rarely play scored games.
q6b: Friendly games with beginners and improvers, or the bottom division of a box league.
q6c: Regular box league or ladder matches in a middle division; I win about half of them.
q6d: The top divisions of my club's box league, or a club team in a county or regional league; I usually beat average league players.
